EBITDA attributable to DMC $10-13M (Q2 8-K Ex.99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034067/000003406726000047/boom-exx991_2026q2.htm, 2026-07-29). Street (one source): revenue $161.1M, EPS $0.11, whisper $0.14 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BOOM, read 2026-10-27). A stale snapshot of the same site, shown in search, carried $154.27M / $0.04. The consensus sits just below the guide midpoint of $163M. The company guide is the bar; the street number has one source and is not used for sizing.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 171,829 shares (prior month 202,385), 0.95% of float, days to cover 1.71 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/boom/statistics/, page dated 2026-10-27, settlement date not shown). Not a crowded short and falling. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline. Put/call OI is 1.44 on only 139 contracts and the ATM spread is 46% of mid, so the option market makes no usable directional statement. Tape: spot $5.38, -4.6% over 20 days, -40% from the 52-week high, +13.7% off the 52-week low. Earnings Whispers puts post-earnings drift at -23.3% since the 2026-07-29 print, which itself traded +15.5%.

evidence.text: The US completions backdrop improved in Q3 2026: the Primary Vision frac spread count averaged about 191.5 in Q3 against about 181.8 in Q2 (+5.4% q/q, roughly +12% y/y). Liberty Energy (2026-10-21) said 'modestly higher completions activity has absorbed much of the industry's available capacity', with 'continued improvement in service pricing' and Q4 seasonality 'partially offset by continued strength in demand'. This supports DynaEnergetics, about 43% of Q2 sales, delivering the sequential increase in the Q3 guide and giving a firmer Q4 tone. The guide had already assumed 'increases in well completion activity', so most of this sits inside it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print (2026-07-29) traded +15.5% on revenue at the top of its range with Dyna +13% q/q, then drifted -23%. Q1 2026 (Dyna -9% y/y) and the Q4 2025 print (2026-02-23) traded -33%. The stock has moved hard on the energy line both ways.
evidence.why_not_priced: The guide assumes higher completions but gives no Dyna dollar figure. If the market had priced a firm Q3/Q4 energy tone, the stock would not have drifted 23% since the last print to within 14% of its 52-week low. Q4 outlook commentary is new information at this release.
evidence.independence: Liberty Energy Q3 2026 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001694028/000169402826000055/q32026-earningsrelease.htm (2026-10-21), a different source. Contradicted in part by Halliburton (finding 3).

evidence.text: Competitive pressure in North American perforating is building against DynaEnergetics. On 2026-09-23, after DMC last spoke, Hunting said Hunting Titan was ranked the No.1 preferred supplier for the second year running (Kimberlite) and pointed to 'growing preference for Hunting Titan's shaped charges and perforating guns in the North American land market'. Hunting's H1 update had already reported Perforating Systems 'significantly ahead of expectations' on North American share gains. On the Q2 call DMC's CEO said 'Pricing is still hard to come by... no price increases, and it's very competitive'. The Q2 Dyna margin of 8.4% (13.4% a year earlier) included a $1.5M tariff refund that is not in the Q3 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints with Dyna margin compression (2025-08-05 at -18.8%, 2025-11-04 at -18.6%) traded heavily down.
evidence.why_not_priced: DMC told the market pricing was tough, so part of this is known. The Sept 23 share-preference data came after DMC last spoke. If the market expected Dyna share loss, consensus revenue ($161.1M) would sit below the guide midpoint by more than $2M. Net of the rest: Arcadia is guided 'steady' and NobelClad up, so a Dyna miss of a few million can still be absorbed in revenue, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: DMC Q2 call (CEO on pricing), https://www.webull.com/news/15364520756012032 (2026-07-29), a different document from Hunting's.

evidence.text: Halliburton's Q3 2026 North America revenue was $2.2B, -5% sequentially, 'primarily driven by lower pressure pumping services in U.S. Land' (reported 2026-10-20). Its early-2027 view assumes a flat North America market with no frac recovery. Read through to perforating-gun demand, this cuts against finding 1. It is one company's share and fleet decisions, and the frac count and Liberty point the other way.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: As for finding 1: the energy line has moved this stock 15-33% at prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a large-cap print, already public for a week. A read-through to a $110M microcap is rarely made explicitly. Sized small as a proxy that a broader series (frac count) partly contradicts.
evidence.independence: Halliburton 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000045012/000004501226000074/hal-20260930.htm (same company, same fact).

evidence.text: The Arcadia minority holder's put on the remaining 40% has been exercisable since 2026-09-06, at a floor value of $187.1M against DMC's market cap of about $110M. DMC can settle in cash, or 20% cash and 80% preferred stock (3% dividend, convertible 1:1, conversion and voting capped at 19.9%, proportionate annual redemptions from 2027-06-23). On the Q2 call the CEO said 'we have absolutely no idea if our partner will stay in the joint venture'. EDGAR shows no 8-K from DMC since the 2026-07-29 print (latest filing a 13G on 2026-08-14), so whether it has been exercised is undisclosed. The Q3 release, 10-Q subsequent-events note or call will very likely address it. The sign is unknowable; this is the largest variance item on the name.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print resolved the put. The December 2024 deferral to September 2026 was described by the CEO as 'immediate and significant relief from the potential equity dilution'.
evidence.why_not_priced: The overhang is public and is a plausible reason for the -23% drift, so the bad case is partly in the price. What the market does not know is the state after Sept 6. That is why this widens [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript, https://www.webull.com/news/15364520756012032 (2026-07-29). EDGAR filing list (no 8-K after 2026-07-29): https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000034067&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

evidence.text: Arcadia's closest listed peer had a steady quarter. Apogee's fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 2026-08-29, overlapping DMC's Q3) showed Architectural Metals sales of $143.5M, +1.8% y/y, gross margin +150bp and a raised full-year EPS guide. That is consistent with DMC's 'steady performance at Arcadia' guide despite DMC's CEO calling commercial construction 'still horrible'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Arcadia (+9% y/y, 13.6% margin) coincided with a +15.5% reaction. Q1 2026 Arcadia (-14% y/y) preceded the weak tape.
evidence.why_not_priced: Apogee's print came after DMC last spoke. A peer read-through is a proxy, and the result sits inside DMC's 'steady' guide, hence small.
evidence.independence: Secondary summary of the Apogee release. https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/apogee-enterprises-reports-q2-fiscal-2027-results shares the same underlying document.

evidence.text: The US Midwest aluminium premium stayed elevated through 2026 (H1 average about 109 c/lb). DMC said higher aluminium prices lifted Arcadia sales and listed 'continued volatility in aluminum input costs' as outside the guide. This should help reported revenue against the $161.1M consensus, with an unknown margin effect. Net zero for the stock.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in the history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Price pass-through lifts the top line, and that is what the print_vs_bar_pct of +1.0 reflects. A revenue beat made of pass-through is low quality, so the stock effect is 0.
evidence.independence: DMC Q2 call on aluminium price effects, https://www.webull.com/news/15364520756012032

evidence.text: Middle East hostilities escalated through the quarter (WTI averaged about $87 in Q3and about $100 into 2026-10-20, per Liberty's 10-Q as summarised). DMC's Q3 guide explicitly 'does not contemplate increased disruptions in international supply chains', and on the Q2 call the CEO cited freight problems at its European operations causing 'timing issues'. This is a risk to Dyna's international and NobelClad shipment timing. Higher oil is a Q4 demand positive, already counted in finding 1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: NobelClad timing has hit prior quarters: Q2 sales were -17% y/y and backlog fell to $63.5M from $70.3M.
evidence.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed; filed as a small proxy.
evidence.independence: DMC Q2 8-K guidance caveat, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034067/000003406726000047/boom-exx991_2026q2.htm

evidence.text: Positioning is light. Short interest is 0.95% of float with 1.7 days to cover and falling. The stock has given back 23% since a +15.5% reaction to the Q2 print and sits 14% above its 52-week low at about 0.6x the Arcadia NCI floor. There is no squeeze fuel, and no crowded long to unwind.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 4 of 7 prior reactions up. The median absolute move is 18.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set itself, not something it misses. A drawdown with a plausible public cause (the put overhang) is worth 0 per [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers PEAD figure, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BOOM

first_hunter_context.bar: Disputed. Q3 2026 adjusted distributable EPS consensus $0.11 per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BRSP/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BRSP), but $0.14 (7 analysts, range $0.13-0.15) per Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BRSP/analysis/). Q2 actual ADE was $0.13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001717547/000171754726000059/brspq226earningsrelease0.htm). There is no company guide, so every size on the name is capped small. print_vs_bar is read against a ~$0.13 midpoint.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is low: about 5.5M shares, 1.96 days to cover at the 2026-06-30 settlement, and about 2.9% of float per an undated Equibles snapshot (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BRSP/short-interest/, https://equibles.com/stocks/BRSP). Not a crowded short. No usable option chain (16 contracts of open interest, put/call OI 0.33), so there is no skew. The stock is -30% since the Q2 print (5.24 to 3.665, Yahoo chart), at 2% above its 52-week low, ~0.54x Q2 GAAP book of $6.81 and ~0.45x undepreciated book of $8.10, with a 17.5% yield on the $0.16 dividend. The whole commercial mREIT group fell with it from Jul 28 to Oct 27 (Yahoo spark): BXMT -37%, TRTX -26%, STWD -25%, ACRE -25%, FBRT -18%, KREF -18%. Activist Cottonwood (CW Investment Advisers) holds 8.7% at an average cost of ~$5.68.

evidence.text: The Albertsons Net Lease 1 sale closed 2026-09-14 for $300.0M ($97.9M net cash plus $200M of debt assumed). The 8-K pro forma shows a gain on sale of $60.4M, about $0.48 per share on ~126.8M shares, and a GAAP equity lift from $862.98M to $923.38M, roughly +$0.47 per share on Q2's $6.81 book value. Q3 GAAP EPS and GAAP book value will therefore print far above the $0.11-0.14 ADE consensus and Q2's -$0.15 GAAP loss, before any Q3 reserve moves.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quarter carried a gain of this size. Q2 2024 had a large GAAP loss (-$0.53) from office equity alongside a dividend cut. The baseline shows the last two prints at -4.58 and -4.45 on ADE and credit, not on GAAP.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pro forma is public, but consensus feeds carry ADE, which excludes realized gains, so the headline GAAP EPS and book value will screen as a large beat and a book increase. If the market had priced a ~7% GAAP book increase, the stock would not have fallen 17% since the 9/16 filing to 0.54x pre-gain book. Economically, much of the gain is depreciation recapture, so undepreciated book (the $8.10 figure management and the activist quote) moves much less. That is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: The sale terms and Q3 closing are corroborated by the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/) and the 8-K item 2.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000171754726000065/brsp-20260914.htm). Both rest on the same transaction.

evidence.text: The loan book grew into Q3: just over $3B in late July (from $2.9B at the Q2 release), with $117M closed after quarter end, $178M in execution, and July originations nearly equal to all of Q2. BRSP then closed the $960M BRSP 2026-FL4 CRE CLO on 2026-10-16 (A notes at SOFR+1.40%) and redeemed the 2024-FL2 CLO with cash on hand. Higher average earning assets support Q3 ADE at or above Q2's $0.13, which beats the $0.11 Benzinga/EW bar and is in line with Yahoo's $0.14. Partial offset: lost Albertsons NOI of ~$10M per half-year, net of 4.77% interest on $200M, for the last ~2 weeks of the quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed $0.13 ADE (a beat on Benzinga, a miss vs Yahoo's $0.15) and the stock went -4.58. Q1 2026 printed $0.14 against higher estimates and the stock went -4.45. This name has not paid for in-line ADE.
evidence.why_not_priced: The bar itself is split ($0.11 vs $0.14), so part of the street is modelling a decline that loan growth argues against. If growth were priced, the stock would not trade at a 17.5% yield. Capped small because the bar is disputed and the name sold its last two ADE prints.
evidence.independence: Q2 call summary on post-quarter closings and the $3.5B year-end target (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/). That is a different document from the CLO 8-K.

evidence.text: Dividend coverage is the open question. Q2 ADE was $0.13 against the $0.16 dividend (81%). Management said the Albertsons sale delays full coverage by about two quarters, to Q2/Q3 2027. At $3.665 the $0.16 quarterly payout yields 17.5%, which prices a cut. The Q3 dividend was already declared on 2026-09-14 and the Q4 one is normally declared mid-December (prior declarations June 15 and Sept 14), so a formal cut is unlikely in this release. But BRSP did announce its 2024 cut ($0.20 to $0.16) inside a Q2 earnings release, and call commentary on the Q4 dividend can move the stock either way.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2024-07-30 release carried the cut to $0.16 alongside a -$0.53 GAAP loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000171754724000068/brspq224earningsreleasev.htm). The baseline does not isolate that day's move.
evidence.why_not_priced: The yield shows a cut is largely priced. Formally reaffirming $0.16 would be a positive surprise, and a cut announced early would still be a negative event: after the 2024 cut the stock carried a lower yield. Sized slightly negative because a lowered payout target is the more likely content, and the reaction to an affirmation is capped by the coverage arithmetic.
evidence.independence: Q3 $0.16 declaration on 2026-09-14 (https://finviz.com/news/391802/brightspire-capital-announces-016-per-share-dividend-for-third-quarter-2026). Q2 2024 cut precedent from a different document (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240730915214/en/brightspire-capital-inc.-announces-second-quarter-2024-financial-results).

evidence.text: Activist and capital return: Cottonwood/CW Investment Advisers (Hon Kit Shing) owns 10.98M shares (8.7%) at an average cost of ~$5.68. Its funds added in Sept at $4.49-4.65. It converted to a 13D on 2026-09-29 after the board twice (Aug 12, Sept 14) refused to waive the 9.8% ownership limit, and it lists a sale, merger, board changes and capitalization proposals as possible actions. BRSP had $29M left on its buyback after buying 3.8M shares at $5.46 in Q2, and received $97.9M of cash from the Albertsons sale. The release and 10-Q cover will show Q3 buyback activity and share count, and the call is the first public venue to answer the 13D.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior activist episode at BRSP. The Q2 'largest buyback in history' quarter still traded -4.58.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell from 4.03 to 3.665 after the 13D was filed, so the market assigns the activist little value. A buyback at ~$4 against $8.10 undepreciated book, or a board response (strategic review, waiver), would be news. Most likely nothing is said, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: Exhibit 1 transactions in the same filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000092189526002666/ex1sc13d14949001_09292026.htm), the same document. Buyback figures from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/).

evidence.text: Financing: on or before 2026-10-19 BRSP redeemed the 2024-FL2 CLO in full with cash on hand, alongside the new $960M FL4 CLO. The money buys a refinanced, larger, match-funded loan book with a 30-month reinvestment period, which corroborates the stated ramp to $3.5B. It also uses cash that could have gone to buybacks, and likely brings an accelerated deferred-financing write-off, a GAAP Q4 item.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FL3 CLO closed in Feb 2026 (redeeming FL1) and that print went +0.52.
evidence.why_not_priced: The filing is public. Its value is in what management says about the funding cost and capacity on the call. It is a financing item that funds visible originations, so it is signed small positive.
evidence.independence: Shares the 8-K with the loan-growth finding, so the two together count once on the CLO fact. That finding rests on the Q2 call, this one on the financing structure.

evidence.text: Sector positioning: the commercial mREIT peer group fell hard from 2026-07-28 to 2026-10-27 (BXMT -37%, TRTX -26%, STWD -25%, ACRE -25%, FBRT -18%, KREF -18%) and BRSP -30%. When the group bounced on 2026-10-22 (TRTX +6.3%, BXMT +3.7%, STWD +3.7%), BRSP rose only +0.8%. The bar for credit commentary is low, but this is a proxy and the name has sold its last two prints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints went -4.58 and -4.45, both into falling sector tapes. The baseline shows 3 of 7 prints up.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is price data, so by definition it is in the price. The only claim is asymmetry: at 0.45x undepreciated book, a quiet credit quarter has more room up than down. It is a proxy, so it carries little weight. The same sector fall also implies peers are seeing credit stress (KREF strategic review, BXMT office defaults), which could show up as more CECL at BRSP.
evidence.independence: KREF strategic review (https://www.credaily.com/briefs/kkr-real-estate-finance-trust-weighs-sale-or-merger-options/?.tsrc=rss) supports the sector-stress reading. No company-level confirmation.

evidence.text: Watch-list and REO items guided for Q3: Mesa AZ multifamily REO sale expected to close in Q3, two multifamily REOs under contract (NAV $62M), the $11M Denver office watch-list loan expected to be sold near term, Austin multifamily and Dallas office loans possibly resolved, the Aurora office net-lease debt maturing in August with an extension under negotiation, and a $57M Las Vegas multifamily loan added to the watch list in Q2. General CECL was already raised to $100M (327 bps).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 resolved three risk-rank-5 loans with a $1M charge-off and the stock went -4.58 on the print.
evidence.why_not_priced: These items are inside what management guided, so they are expected. Only a surprise (Aurora default, new risk-rank 5s) would move the stock, and nothing public points to one. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: None beyond the same call.

evidence.text: Q4 dividend declaration, normally mid-December (Q2 declared June 15, Q3 Sept 14). The formal cut-or-hold decision most likely lands then.
Cottonwood 13D escalation: possible proposals on board composition or a sale, with timing undated.
Earnings Whispers listing the report on November 2, 2026
AAII article describing $0.13 as Q3 earnings
Short interest ratio of 6.5 days (MarketBeat)
Analyst price-target or rating changes dated Aug-Oct 2026: none found; the latest are the July 30 cuts (B. Riley $6.50, BofA $5.25 Underperform).

evidence.text: SEIA/Wood Mackenzie's Q3 2026 Solar Market Insight (published September 2026, after Enphase's July 28 call) shows US residential Q2 installs at 995 MW: -12% YoY, -10% QoQ, the lowest in five years. evidence.text: The Q4 bar is demanding against the safe-harbor mix. FY2026 consensus revenue is $1.18B (S&P Global via stockanalysis). evidence.text: The FY26 10-K shows remaining performance obligations of $833.0m at 2026-06-30, up 15.7% YoY, after four straight quarters of 26-27% YoY growth (Jun-25 $719.7m +27.0%, Dec-25 $777.1m +26.3%, Mar-26 $791.4m +27.3%); the Q4 sequential add was $41.6m against $98.2m a year earlier. The Q1 10-Q, normally filed the same day as the release, will show Sep-26 RPO. Q1 is seasonally flat (Sep-25 was $715.2m, -$4.5m QoQ), so a repeat puts YoY RPO growth near 16%, which would confirm the deceleration. The market's expectation sits on cloud ARR growth of about 29%, not on RPO.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: RPO has not been a headline line in any of the last six reactions in the baseline; the Aug 4 2026 +12.75% reaction preceded the 10-K (Aug 14) in which the deceleration first appeared, and the stock has risen roughly 15% since that filing without it being cited anywhere found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Intapp reports ARR and NRR as headline KPIs, and RPO appears only in the 10-K/10-Q revenue note. No preview, target change or article found since Aug 14 mentions it. If it were priced, some analyst note in the October target raises (Barclays to $38, UBS to $46) would cite backlog. It is partly explained, which caps the size: on the Aug 4 call the CFO said many on-prem clients are shortening contracts to one year or less ahead of cloud migration. That compresses multi-year license RPO without implying weaker cloud demand.
evidence.independence: Same company documents. CFO commentary on shortened on-prem terms and license revenue -25% in Q4 (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945294) explains rather than corroborates it. evidence.text: Intapp habitually prints above the top of its own quarterly guide. Q4 FY26 total revenue was $152.5m against $149.1-150.1m (+1.9% vs the midpoint), SaaS $115.0m against $113.1-114.1m, and non-GAAP EPS $0.41 against $0.36-0.38. A repeat on the Q1 guide (total $159.3-160.3m, SaaS $123.7-124.7m, EPS $0.39-0.41) implies about $162m total, about $125.5m SaaS (+29% YoY vs $97.5m), and about $0.43 EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats of a similar size drew +12.75% (Aug 4 2026, $0.41 vs $0.36 plus a guide above consensus) and -4.19% (May 5 2026, beat by $0.01). The headline beat alone has not set the sign; the guide and cloud ARR have.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. A modest beat inside the company's own pattern is what the Street models, so this lands inside what the company guided and should be sized toward 0. It is filed because a judge needs the effective bar: a print merely at the guide midpoint would read as a miss.
evidence.independence: Q4 actuals from the Aug 4 2026 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001565687/000156568726000065/inta-20260630xex991.htm), a different document from the Q4 guide in the May 5 release.

evidence.text: The stock ran +30.6% in 20 sessions, from $37.60 on Oct 7 to a $48.01 high on Oct 23, on a sector-wide software rerating with no company-specific catalyst found. It now trades at $46, above the average analyst target of $39.14; Barclays raised its target only to $38 at Underweight on Oct 12. Short interest is 4% of float and falling, so there is no squeeze bid to cushion a disappointment. The setup asks Q1 to justify a rerating rather than to clear the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline does not record pre-print run-ups. The Feb 3 2026 print fell -13.2% after the stock had held up into the sector's AI-disruption sell-off. Six-print history: 2 up, 4 down, median absolute move 9.67%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is public, so this is about asymmetry, not hidden information. Skew is flat (-0.09) and put/call OI is 0.26, so options are not paying for downside after a 30% move. If the market were braced for a sell-the-news reaction, puts would be bid. The sector move was index-led: the software index hit 2026 highs on Oct 6 as AI-disruption fears faded. That makes INTA's extra rise a beta re-rating that a soft cloud ARR number or an unraised FY guide would test.
evidence.independence: Sector context from Reuters via US News, 2026-10-06 (https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-10-06/us-software-stocks-scale-fresh-2026-highs-as-ai-disruption-worries-fade); Barclays Underweight with a $38 target on 2026-10-12 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/barclays-lifts-target-for-intapp-stock-to-usd-38-00/70333435); short interest from MarketBeat's short-interest page. first_hunter_context.bar: Company guide from the 9 Sep 2026 Q2 release: Q3 same-store sales +3.0% to +4.0%, Q3 adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 13%; FY26 same-store sales +2.5% to +3.0%, net unit growth of at least 8%, adjusted EBITDA growth of at least 20% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000212704326000008/q22026earningsrelease.htm). The EPS consensus is disputed: Benzinga shows $0.08 and Stocktwits $0.15, and both carry a revenue figure ($208.6M) equal to Q2's actual, so it is probably mislabelled. Every EPS-dependent size is therefore capped small; the same-store-sales and EBITDA bars are company-sourced.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 11,184,307 shares on the 2026-10-15 settlement (FINRA published 10-26), down 10.6% from 12.51M on 9-30, which was up from 2.90M on 7-31. Days to cover 3.7. Aggregators report 3.5% of float, but they divide by about 317.6M fully exchanged shares (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/JMKE/short-interest/). The freely traded float is far smaller: Blackstone affiliates pledged 127.6M of the roughly 233.4M Class A shares (8-K, 2026-09-22) and ADIA holds 35.7M (13G, event date 2026-09-30), which leaves about 70M Class A shares (my inference), including the 46.05M IPO plus over-allotment shares. On that basis the short is about 16-24% of tradeable shares. Skew is +9.69 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest 0.35, ATM spread 25.5% of mid. Equibles reports 6 insider buyers and no sellers over 90 days (net +$1.0M).

evidence.text: Q3 same-store sales were guided at +3.0% to +4.0% on 9 Sep 2026, about ten of the quarter's thirteen weeks in (Q2 ended 28 Jun, so Q3 ended about 27 Sep). The release said the acceleration from Q1 +1.7% to Q2 +2.3%, which was transaction-led, 'has continued into the third quarter', and a call summary has the quarter-to-date run above 3%. The reported comp is therefore close to pre-determined inside the guide, with a lean to the middle or upper half; the bar is the 3.5% midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print as a public company. Q2 comps of +2.3% (accelerating, transaction-led) were bought +7.44% on the day, 9 Sep, then fully retraced within about three weeks to a 30% drawdown. The baseline history is flagged untrustworthy as a base rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, which is why it is sized small: it lands inside the company's own guide. What is not obviously priced is that the stock fell about 30% after a release saying comps were accelerating into Q3. A market that trusted the guide would not have taken the stock 25% below the IPO price with targets cut. In-line or upper-half comps confirm a number the price behaves as if it doubts.
evidence.independence: The 'tracking above 3%' quarter-to-date remark is a MarketBeat summary of the same call, not a separate source (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-jersey-mikes-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-09/; when fetched, that URL served a different page). Subway's 729 net US closures in 2025 support continued category share gain (https://www.ktvu.com/news/subway-closes-locations-2025).

evidence.text: The consumer backdrop worsened after the 9 Sep guide was set. Placer.ai's August 2026 index had US dining visits down 2.4% YoY, with gasoline above $4 and food-away-from-home prices up 3.4%. September CPI printed 3.7% against 3.6% expected, and restaurant stocks fell 3-4% on 14 Oct. Domino's Q3 2026 US comps were +0.3% against +5.2% a year earlier (13 Oct). Fast-casual visits decelerated to +1.9% in Q3 from +2.2% in Q2. This bears on the Q4 implied guide and the FY same-store-sales range of 2.5-3.0% rather than on the locked Q3 number.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No guidance change yet as a public company: on 9 Sep the FY comp range was maintained and the stock rose 7.4%. Peers: Domino's fell about 3% pre-market on its comp slowdown (https://finviz.com/news/401785/dominos-pizza-beats-third-quarter-earnings-estimates-but-shares-fall-as-same-store-sales-growth-slows).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector sold off on these prints. The FY guide has not yet been restated against them, and Jersey Mike's has said it is outgrowing industry traffic, so whether the macro reaches its Q4 implied comp is unknown. If the market had fully priced a cut, sell-side targets would have moved below $22 (the lowest is TD Cowen's $22).
evidence.independence: This is a macro and peer proxy, not company data, and the company's own Q2 number (comps accelerating while industry traffic fell) argues against it, so it is sized small. The Domino's comp is from Domino's own release, a different source (https://www.franchising.com/news/20261013_dominos_pizza_announces_third_quarter_2026_financial_results.html). Chipotle visits +6.0% (Placer, via NACS) points the other way for one strong brand (https://convenience.org/stay-current/news/2026/october/19/chipotle-is-outpacing-greater-qsr-segment).

evidence.text: The FY adjusted EBITDA guide of at least +20% is back-loaded. Q1 was +50% (to $84M) and Q2 +7% (to $114M, +18% excluding a $10M adverse ad-fund timing hit), so H1 is about +22%. With Q3 guided at 'at least 13%', Q4 has to grow well above 20% to hold the FY floor (my inference; the H2-2025 base is not disclosed). The 10-Q shows a $7M year-to-date ad-fund deficit (advertising expense $115M against revenue $108M) that should reverse, and Area Director buyouts ($52M YTD) mechanically add royalty EBITDA. The FY floor is the line at risk of a trim.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 9 Sep reported adjusted EBITDA growth was only 7% and the stock still rose 7.4%. The market accepted the timing explanation that day, then de-rated the stock over the following weeks.
evidence.why_not_priced: The back-half arithmetic is not in any preview found. Previews quote the guide ranges only, with no Q3 or Q4 EBITDA split, so a trim or a firming of the 20% floor would be new information either way.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2 release and 10-Q with finding 1. The ad-fund reversal and the trim risk point opposite ways inside one document, so the net is sized near zero.

evidence.text: Positioning into the print is washed out. The stock is at $17.26, 25% below the $23 IPO price and 29% below its post-Q2 high. Short interest went from 2.9M shares at IPO to 11.2M on 15 Oct (DTC 3.7), which is roughly 16-24% of the shares that actually trade once Blackstone's pledged 127.6M and ADIA's 35.7M are removed, against 3.5% on the aggregators' fully exchanged base. Meanwhile 21 of 27 analysts rate it Buy with a $27.78 average target, despite target cuts from JPM and Jefferies (29 Sep), TD Cowen to $22 (7 Oct) and Raymond James to $26 (16 Oct).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The single prior print (+7.44%) came with short interest rising from 7.5M to 10.4M over 31 Aug to 15 Sep. A comp acceleration print was bought that day.
evidence.why_not_priced: Aggregators print 3.5% of float because they divide by the fully exchanged share count, so screens do not flag this as a crowded short. If the true-float crowding were recognised, the skew would not be paying +9.7 vol points for downside on a name whose put/call open interest is 0.35.
evidence.independence: Float arithmetic rests on the Blackstone pledge 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000119312526397249/ck0002127043-20260916.htm) and the ADIA 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000110465926118565/primary_doc.xml). Analyst actions are from https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/JMKE/forecast/. This cuts against the +9.69 put skew; sized down for that.

evidence.text: Blackstone affiliates hold about $1.09B of Morgan Stanley margin loans secured on 127.6M Class A shares plus 45.0M Class B shares and units, about 54.3% of the fully exchanged Class A (8-K Items 5.01/8.01, closing 16 Sep, filed 22 Sep). The company agreed not to hinder lender foreclosure. At $17.26 the implied LTV is about 29% (my arithmetic), so this is not a near-term margin call, but it is a standing supply overhang that caps rallies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 4.2% on 21 Sep, the session before the 8-K; it was $20.67 on 15 Sep and $16.86 on 30 Sep.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since the 30% drawdown followed it (Forbes, 25 Oct: 'Blackstone may keep buyers away'). It is filed because it shapes the reaction function: upside on a good print is capped by known supply. Asked what the money buys: it is sponsor liquidity, not company funding, so it is a negative overhang rather than a company-distress signal.
evidence.independence: Forbes 2026-10-25 makes the same argument (https://www.forbes.com/sites/jimosman/2026/10/25/jersey-mikes-stock-fell-30-and-blackstone-may-keep-buyers-away/, snippet only). The Boardwalk ML Holdco Form 4 of 2 Oct is a margin-loan holdco transfer, not a sale (accession 0001193125-26-412417).

evidence.text: IPO proceeds of $301M repaid $46M of Series 2026-1 notes and $255M of Series 2026-1A notes on 17 Aug 2026, at a weighted-average rate of about 5.18%. That is roughly $3.9M a quarter of interest saved, and Q3 is the first quarter carrying most of it, which helps the GAAP and adjusted EPS line.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: there is no prior EPS reaction to separate from the comp line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The EPS bar is disputed ($0.08 against $0.15), so it is unclear whether estimates include the paydown; capped small because the bar is unsourced. The company guided Q3 net interest expense at $28M (per Equibles), so it is likely inside guidance.
evidence.independence: Shares the 10-Q with finding 3.

evidence.text: The 180-day IPO lock-up for Blackstone, ADIA and management expires about 2027-01-26 (IPO 30-31 Jul 2026). Per a secondary source; the S-1 was not verified.
An earn-out of up to $250M is payable to pre-IPO holders on the 4,000th store (3,378 at Q2) or on a change in control.
